title: Clock and Bridge
premise: In 1898, in a river port whose fortunes hang on a single toll bridge, sixteen-year-old Wendell Almeida — indentured to the Marrow & Vane Trading Company since her pearl-diver father drowned in their debt — keeps the company's ledgers and believes history is something that happens elsewhere. When the bridge closes for the flood season, she discovers the ledgers hide a deliberate falsification: the company has been buying divers' debts with forged signatures, including her father's, to seize their boats and silence a drowning-accident inquiry. With the company's owners sailing out on the morning tide to bury the evidence abroad, Wendell must rally the indebted families, copy the true records, and get sworn testimony before a visiting magistrate who may himself be bought. She wins the truth on the record at terrible cost — the bridge burns in the owners' desperation, her indenture is voided only because she is charged alongside them, and justice arrives not as vindication but as survival: the ship sails without its cargo of secrets, and Wendell, free but unmoored, begins writing the account we have just read.
about_author: Ada Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from colonial river ports before turning to fiction. She writes about people history recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Toll of Small Things
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A day in the counting house: she balances ledgers, endures the clerk Brannigan's contempt, and visits her mother among the diver families on the mudflats. The emotional beat is quiet resignation — Wendell has made peace with smallness, believing the bridge, the river, and her life will simply continue as they are.

chapters.title: Water Over the Road
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The flood season closes the bridge; the last packet boat leaves, stranding the town with Marrow & Vane's owners, the Vane cousins, aboard their anchored ship awaiting the tide. That night Wendell finds a ledger page where her father's signature appears on a debt contract dated after his drowning. The beat: dread cracking open routine.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with a flashback chapter from her father's diving days woven through her memory. She compares signatures across three years of ledgers and finds a pattern: every dead or drowned diver 'signed' away his boat. She confides in Old Sef, the bridge keeper, who warns her that paper obeys whoever holds it. Beat: fear hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Cousins' Dinner
chapters.summary: Wendell serves at a company dinner and hears the Vanes plan to sail at dawn with all records aboard, ahead of a magistrate arriving by river next week. Brannigan catches her lingering; suspicion blooms. Beat: claustrophobia — the enemy is at the table, smiling, and time is measured in tides now.

chapters.title: Debts of the Living
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Wendell and Tomas Iriarte, a young diver whose family boat was seized. Wendell shows him the forged signature of his uncle; Tomas wants to burn the counting house tonight. Wendell argues for the record, not the flame — testimony the magistrate must witness. Beat: fragile alliance across old resentments between ledger-keepers and divers.

chapters.title: The Bridge Keeper's Oath
chapters.summary: Old Sef's POV. He reveals he watched the first forgery happen years ago and stayed silent for his pension; he gives Wendell the key to the company's archive room and his own sworn statement. Beat: guilt transmuted into courage — an old man choosing, too late but finally, which side of history to stand on.

chapters.title: Night Copying
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She, Tomas, and two others spend one night copying incriminating pages while Brannigan works late below, forcing them to freeze by lamplight. They finish as dawn greys; Wendell hides the originals inside the bridge's toll chest. Beat: terror and exhilaration — the truth now exists in more than one pair of hands.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The Vanes discover the theft; men come for Wendell, and in the chaos a lantern takes the toll house — then the bridge itself begins to burn, the only road out dying above the flooded river. Sef dies saving the toll chest. Beat: catastrophe; the price of survival made literal, and Wendell arrested alongside the divers.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Morning
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, from a cell, as the magistrate arrives to find a burned bridge, a jailed girl, and a company demanding her head. Wendell bargains: her testimony and the salvaged originals against charges on everyone. The Vanes try to sail early, but the burned bridge has fouled the channel with debris. Beat: climax — words versus money, spoken aloud on the record.

chapters.title: What the Tide Carries Out
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Vanes sail in disgrace under investigation; the ship leaves lighter than it came. Her indenture is voided, Sef is buried, Tomas rebuilds, and the town must decide whether the new bridge will be theirs. Wendell buys ink with her first free wages and begins writing. Beat: bittersweet resolution — justice partial, freedom real, history finally hers to hold.
